components.howToRender: Import SessionCard directly and render it with fixture InboxSession objects inside <div data-sv-rail className="bg-sol-bg-alt">. The hover gradient assumes --sol-bg-alt ground, and [data-sv-rail] is the hook the globals.css compact rules key on. Mount it client-only behind a mounted gate or Suspense, because of the missing getServerSnapshot, and keep the productMocks poster for the prerender. Keep the fixtures local: useState rows, onSelect/onPin/onDismiss/onStash wired to local state. Passing onPin/onDismiss/onStash shows the real hover toolbar, and pinning then works purely locally by flipping is_pinned in fixture state. Then guard the few hard-wired store and server paths with a wrapper: onClickCapture/onDragStartCapture that preventDefault+stopPropagation on the star button ([aria-label=Favorite]), the Tag button, anchors and the comment chip, or just omit those fields (leave assigned_ping, open_comment_threads, spawned_by_conversation_id, role, is_anchor, owner_device_id, image_preview_url and git remote/branch unset, or set git_branch only if BranchCodeLink clicks are captured). Use non-Convex-looking ids (e.g. 'hero-1'). Build timestamps relative to Date.now() at mount. To get the green working ping, set agent_status:'working', agent_status_updated_at/last_heartbeat≈now, producing_until in the future, message_count>0, and check it with sessionLiveAt (lib/liveness.ts:60). A NEEDS INPUT or DONE chip comes from thread_state + thread_state_status (lib/threadState.ts:113). Use idle_summary or subtitle for the summary line and last_user_message for the '>' line. Pass isUnread for the cyan dot plus bold title. Pass variant='working' for the green-tinted row. Pass isActive for the cyan active treatment. To stop viewer prefs from leaking in, you cannot override clientState through props. Better: refactor the card so a thin wrapper reads the store and passes prefs down, leaving a pure SessionCardView. As it stands, the hero inherits the viewer's show_agent_icon, personify and branch prefs. The import cost is large: GlobalSessionPanel.tsx is 5.2k lines with ~100 imports (ConversationDiffLayout lazy, triggers, org, etc.). Consider moving SessionCard into its own module, or lazy-load the hero's real-UI layer after the poster.

These map to var(--sol-*) through color-mix (tailwind.config.ts:65-75). (2) Accent classes are hardcoded Solarized hex regardless of theme: text-sol-cyan/blue/violet/green/yellow/red/magenta/amber (tailwind.config.ts:47-64). SessionCard also uses a few raw hues: text-gray-400/500, sky-700 with a dark: sky-300 for the '>' prompt, violet-400/500, amber-400. It also uses inline var(--sol-bg-alt) and var(--sol-cyan) inside color-mix for the hover fade (2459). The light palette is the :root default in app/globals.css:326 (--sol-bg #FBF5E2, --sol-bg-alt #eee8d5, etc.). .dark (387) overrides it, and .minimal-style (407) overrides it again with a white/grey palette and SF Pro --font-ui. The marketing page does load all of this. globals.css is imported once in src/main.tsx:2 for every route. MarketingLayout (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx) mounts ForceLightMode (components/force-light-mode.tsx), which swaps html.dark for html.light and restores the saved theme on unmount, and it paints #fdf6e3 behind the page. It also sets --user-bubble hue on html (45). Fix this by scoping a wrapper that re-declares the :root light --sol-* values (or by having ForceLightMode also strip minimal-style). (b) The .light class on the MarketingLayout div defines no variables; everything cascades from :root. (c) Simple-view and inbox-compact restyles key on shell classes that DashboardLayout adds (DashboardLayout.tsx:432), so they are absent on marketing, which is good: the cards show the default layout. notes:
Bottom line: the only real inbox component worth mounting as-is is SessionCard (GlobalSessionPanel.tsx:1952). Everything around it (SessionListPanel, Sidebar, GlobalSearch, the DashboardLayout header, LabelChipsRow) is wired to the live store, feeders and queries and can't take fixtures without writing them into the visitor's real inboxStore. That is the leak you must avoid, because store writes go to IDB and dispatch.

Current state: the hero today (app/(marketing)/HeroFlythrough.tsx → heroFly/surfaces.tsx) renders hand-built mocks from app/(marketing)/productMocks.tsx: SessionRow at 113, HeroSidebar at 79, HERO_SESSIONS at 68, with hardcoded hex colours (INK/DIM/BODY in surfaces.tsx:66-68). This is the 'placeholder stuff' to replace.

Recommended path, in order:
1. Make SessionCard safe to feed. Split it into a pure SessionCardView that takes prefs, viewer id, roster and the handler callbacks as props, plus the existing store-reading wrapper. The inbox and the hero then share one component, and viewer prefs can't leak. Without the split, the hero inherits the visitor's show_agent_icon, personify_sessions, show_branch_pill and inbox_image_thumbs prefs.
2. Move SessionCard out of the 5.2k-line GlobalSessionPanel.tsx into its own module so Landing doesn't pull the whole inbox graph.
3. Export the Sidebar primitives (RailHeading, SectionRow, NavCount, NavSection at Sidebar.tsx:99-376). Extract the inline Inbox nav row (1282-1306), the SessionListPanel section-header button (renderSection, ~4499) and a pure search field from GlobalSearch. Then build the hero rail, panel head and top bar from real components instead of copies.
4. Render the real layer client-only. useTrackedStore has no getServerSnapshot (store/inboxStore.ts:12956), and Landing is prerendered with renderToString (src/prerender-entry.tsx), which would throw. Keep a static poster for SSR and swap in the real components after mount.

Guards needed even after the split:
- Capture clicks on the star (toggleFavorite, 2609), Tag (openPalette, 3040), comment chip (requestNavigate, 2861), 'Got it' (ack mutation, 2665), and every next Link (BranchCodeLink, /org/..). The compat Link respects preventDefault (src/compat/next-link.tsx:17-18).
- Capture dragstart (startPaneDrag, 2311) and file drops (the upload mutations).
- Keep hero ids non-Convex-shaped. Leave role, anchor and device fields unset so RoleHoverCard's useQueryNoThrow(api.org.roleCard) never fires.
- Nothing in SessionCard registers keyboard shortcuts or analytics. GlobalSearch does register one (search.open, GlobalSearch.tsx:165), which is another reason not to mount it.

Safe light interactions:
- Hover shows the real hover toolbar when you pass the on* handlers.
- Local pin toggling (flip is_pinned in fixture state via onPin).
- onSelect switches the active card (cyan treatment).
- Toggling isUnread.
- InboxViewMenu's real popover with local state.
- Section collapse, once the header is extracted.

Fixture fields that light up real states:
- Working ping: agent_status 'working' with fresh agent_status_updated_at, last_heartbeat and producing_until, and message_count > 0.
- Status chips: thread_state + thread_state_status give the NEEDS INPUT and DONE chips and the pin line.
- Text lines: idle_summary or subtitle, and last_user_message.
- Meta row: worktree_name, pr_status, active_task/active_plan {title}, and git_root/project_path for the project dot. Project colours come from getLabelColor.
- Blocked chip: pending_api_error_kind.
- Subagent compact row: is_subagent.
- Clock: build every timestamp from Date.now() at mount, because the card formats idle time relative to now.

theme:
How the colours arrive: nearly every block paints with Tailwind `sol-*` classes. The neutral ones (bg, bg-alt, card, border, text, text-muted, text-dim and so on) are `themed('--sol-*')` colour-mix lookups on CSS variables (packages/web/tailwind.config.ts:18-75). The accent classes (sol-yellow, green, red, blue, violet, cyan and so on) are hardcoded Solarized hex (tailwind.config.ts:47-64), so they look the same in every theme. The variables are set in packages/web/app/globals.css: light values on `:root` (326-385), dark values on `.dark` (387-405), and a white/grey palette with an SF font on `.minimal-style` (407-420, plus `.dark.minimal-style` at 474). `darkMode: ["class"]` is set (tailwind.config.ts:28), but these blocks barely use `dark:` variants (2 in toolBlocks.tsx, none in the others), so theme is almost entirely a question of which class sits on `<html>`. The cast-canvas shadow root reads `var(--sol-*)` and `--font-mono` from its host (HtmlSnippet.tsx:36-47), so it follows whatever theme the hero is in. Code blocks use the `--hljs-*` variables.

Does the marketing page load it? Yes. globals.css is imported once in src/main.tsx:2 for every route, and index.html loads JetBrains Mono and Fraunces. So the real components get their styling on `/`.

Is it light mode? Usually, but not reliably:
1. `ForceLightMode` (components/force-light-mode.tsx) swaps `dark` for `light` on `<html>` when the page mounts. It never removes `minimal-style`, so a signed-in user with the minimal visual style sees the product blocks in the white/grey palette and SF font.
2. `ThemeProvider` (components/ThemeProvider.tsx, the effect after `useMountEffect`) runs `classList.remove("dark","light"); add(theme)` every time `theme` changes. `theme` is `clientState.ui.theme ?? localStorage`, so if the synced setting lands after the marketing page mounted and differs from localStorage, `html.dark` comes back.
3. MarketingLayout's wrapper `<div className="light">` (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx) sets no variables: globals.css has no `.light` token rule (the only `.light` hit, line 5034, is unrelated), so it cannot protect the hero.
4. The marketing page background is `#fdf6e3`, but light `--sol-bg` is `#FBF5E2`, so real `bg-sol-bg` surfaces are a shade off the page.

Recommendation: give the hero root a scoped token class that re-declares the light `--sol-*` and `--hljs-*` values and `--font-ui: var(--font-mono)`. It should be one class in globals.css that reuses the `:root` block rather than a copy. Nested inside the hero, it beats `.dark` and `.minimal-style` for everything below it. Shadow-DOM canvases inherit it too.

notes:
What I found (read-only, nothing edited):

1. There is no fixture layer today. The current hero (app/(marketing)/heroFly/surfaces.tsx, 733 lines) is all hand-built mocks with hex colours. `useInboxStore` is one shared module-level store (store/inboxStore.ts:12843) that every component imports directly, so a fixture store cannot be swapped in while the page runs. The one existing real-components-on-fixtures precedent, vite.preview-migrate.config.ts:18-47, replaces modules at build time, which a live marketing page cannot use. The safe path is therefore: render the leaf blocks, and leave out every prop that opens a data path.

2. The main rule: leave out conversationId everywhere. UserPrompt, AssistantBlock, ToolBlock and CastCommandBlock gate their queries, MessageReview, MessageIdentityProvider, store-backed bookmarks, pending-status sync and repository lookups on it (turnBlocks.tsx:246, 264, 1403; toolBlocks.tsx ~739). Without it, their dependencies shrink to read-only store selectors that return nothing for fixture ids. Also leave out isPending, storage_id, onForkFromMessage and the share callbacks, and conversation_id on permissions.

3. Four places break isolation even so, and each needs a one-site fix:
   - EntityIdPill resolution (lib/entityDisplay.ts:170) runs real webGet queries. For signed-in users, a fixture short id can resolve to their real data. Clicking a resolved session pill calls syncRecord on the persisted store (hooks/useOpenLinkedSession.ts:64-72). Fix: a fixture-context override inside useEntityResolution, with castBlocks.tsx's own webGet queries (57, 82, 104-106) routed through that hook.
   - PermissionStack (PermissionCard.tsx:114) fires a real mutation, writes the store and listens for y/n on window. Fix: split it into a presentational view plus a container.
   - MessageInput writes drafts and sends. Fix: extract ComposerShell.
   - The header is inline in ConversationView. Fix: extract ConversationHeaderBar and AgentStatusPill, which also removes the four-times-repeated status ternary.

4. Wrap the whole hero in three guards:
   - `RevealInBandCtx.Provider value={true}`, which turns off reveal bands that would mount real RoutePane/SessionPane.
   - An `onClickCapture` that cancels anchor navigation. Things that must stay interactive (Approve, palette typing) should be fixture-driven views, not the real handlers.
   - No ImageGalleryProvider, no HighlightContext, no ShortcutTooltip `action`s that matter.

5. Global side effects to know about:
   - Radix hover cards and popovers, ContextMenu, and every fullscreen view portal to document.body. They show up flat, outside the 3D world, in screen coordinates.
   - AvatarImg writes fixture avatar bytes into the shared Cache Storage 'codecast:avatars:v1'. It is harmless, but use same-origin static paths.
   - Clicking an Edit tool row sets diffViewerStore, which is the app's panel state but is not persisted.
   - Toasts go through the global sonner Toaster.
   - The app's Providers (src/providers.tsx) are already mounted on `/`: ConvexAuthRoot, ThemeProvider, ShortcutProvider, TipProvider, Toaster. So useQuery, useRouter (compat shim src/compat/next-navigation.ts) and ShortcutTooltip all work there, and the store is already booted on the marketing page for every visitor. Importing it adds no runtime cost.

6. Prerender risk. The landing page is SSR-prerendered by src/prerender-entry.tsx, which provides only ConvexProviderWithAuth and a MemoryRouter: no ShortcutProvider, no ThemeProvider. The landing's import graph does not currently touch store/inboxStore. Importing the blocks pulls in the store, which calls bootPersistence() at module load (inboxStore.ts:13471), plus react-markdown, rehype-highlight and the Convex api into the SSR build. Recommendation: mount the real-component layer client-only after hydration, keeping the prerendered and reduced-motion poster from static markup. Or verify that `scripts/prerender.mjs` still passes.

7. Determinism. formatRelativeTime and WorkingStatusLine read Date.now(), so fixture timestamps must be computed relative to mount time. The 'N ago' labels and the working clock do not follow the timeline t that the spec requires; the spec wants typing and counters to be pure functions of t, so drive those labels from the timeline.

8. Message shapes (conversation/types.ts):
   - ToolCall {id, name, input: JSON string}
   - ToolResult {tool_use_id, content, is_error?}
   - ImageData {media_type, data? | preview_url? | storage_id?, tool_use_id?}
   - Message (line 38) {_id, role, content, timestamp, thinking?, tool_calls?, tool_results?, images?, model?}

   How each fixture reaches its renderer:
   - Cast rows are Bash tool calls with input {command: 'cast ...'} (classify.ts:240).
   - Subagent spawns are Agent/Task tool calls with {subagent_type, description, prompt}.
   - 'Message from' cards are user messages classified as session_message.
   - Canvases are ```cast-canvas fences in the assistant content.

9. Theme: see the theme field. It is mostly light via ForceLightMode, but minimal-style leaks through and ThemeProvider can re-add dark. Add one hero-scoped light-token class that reuses the :root values.

theme:
Colors come from Tailwind classes. The neutral surface and text classes (bg-sol-bg, bg-sol-bg-alt, bg-sol-card, border-sol-border, text-sol-text, text-sol-text-muted, text-sol-text-dim) resolve to CSS variables (--sol-bg etc.) through tailwind.config themed() (tailwind.config.*:65-75). The accent classes are hardcoded hex (text-sol-yellow is #b58900 and text-sol-blue is #268bd2 at :56,62; cyan is an rgb), so accents never follow the theme. The variables are declared on :root as Solarized Light (globals.css:326-337, --sol-bg #FBF5E2) and overridden by `.dark` (:387, #002b36) and `.minimal-style` (:406, white surfaces, and --font-ui switched to SF Pro). A few components also use Tailwind `dark:` variants (darkMode: ['class']), e.g. KanbanCard's 'bg-white dark:bg-sol-bg-alt' and PlanTaskSection's 'text-gray-400 dark:text-gray-500'.

The marketing page does load the app's globals.css: src/main.tsx:2 imports it for every route. The landing route renders under MarketingLayout (src/App.tsx:168, src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx), which mounts ForceLightMode (components/force-light-mode.tsx: removes dark/light from <html> and adds 'light') and a wrapper div with class 'light'. Neither globals.css nor anything else defines a `.light` variable scope; the only hit is a .light.minimal-style rule at :5034. Light mode therefore holds only while <html> lacks `.dark`. There are three gaps for signed-in users:
(1) ForceLightMode never removes `minimal-style`, which index.html:39-41 and ThemeProvider.tsx:77 add. A user on the minimal visual style would see the real components on the white or grey minimal palette and in SF Pro instead of JetBrains Mono.
(2) Likely but unverified: ThemeProvider (components/ThemeProvider.tsx:50-56) re-adds the stored theme class whenever `theme` or `mounted` changes. ThemeProvider renders null until mounted, so its [theme, mounted] effect runs in the same commit that first mounts MarketingLayout. React flushes passive effects child-first, so the parent's effect would run after ForceLightMode's and put `dark` back for a dark-theme user. A later clientState.ui.theme sync would re-add `dark` the same way. Today's marketing page wouldn't show this because it paints with inline hex.
(3) Anything that portals to body (HoverCard and Popover for role cards and entity pills, the sonner Toaster) sits outside any wrapper you add.
Recommendation: give the hero stage its own light scope that re-declares the :root --sol-* block (light values, --font-ui: var(--font-mono)), e.g. a `.sol-light-scope` class derived from the same source as :root so the values aren't copied by hand. Variables cascade, so the real components render Solarized Light inside the stage regardless of the html classes. Also import components/editor/editor.css (doc title and read body) and components/threads/threads.css if TaskCommentStream's th-* classes are used. JetBrains Mono comes from the index.html Google Fonts link, which is fine.
notes:
Isolation facts that decide the approach:
- The store is a single module-level singleton (store/inboxStore.ts:12843 `useInboxStore = survivingInboxStore ?? createInboxStore()`). There is no provider or context to swap in a fixture store, and useTrackedStore reads useInboxStore directly (:12954). Reading fixture ids from the real store is harmless: taskActiveSessions, sessionDecisions, workflowRuns and reviewComments all come back empty, so TaskDecisionChip and TaskLineChip render nothing. The dangers are writes. Every action() or sync() in these components writes the real draft, and sync()/action() persist to IDB, and action() also dispatches to the server. The write points in this surface: TaskRow's ItemRowState callbacks (safe because you supply them); ActiveSessionBadge click (openSidePanel); DocRow star (pinDoc); PlanTaskSection status/priority/title/add (updateTask, createTask); PlanBoardView drag (updateTask, closeTaskWithGuard); TeamShareChip (only with shareTeamId); MessageReview block quoting (addReviewComment, persisted to IDB meta, clientSyncRegistry.ts:871); ContextChatInput submit; SlotActions (wsHide, router.push); GenericListView (storeOpenPalette plus shortcut registration via useShortcutAction, GenericListView.tsx:875). Wherever the hero wants interactivity, use components whose effects arrive through props (TaskRow via ItemRowState, FeedCard via onNavigate, TaskTimeline filter, PlanProgressBar), and put an onClickCapture/onPointerDownCapture guard or pointer-events:none on the rest.
- Convex: none of the recommended leaves query on mount with fixture data, provided fixture markdown and event refs contain no entity ids. Any ct-/pl-/sd-/op- short id or 32-char Convex id in markdown becomes an EntityIdPill that subscribes to tasks.webGet, plans.webGet, docs.webGet, entities.resolveIdType and others (lib/entityDisplay.ts:184-200). For anonymous visitors tasks.webGet returns null (convex/tasks.ts webGet: `if (!userId) return null`), but these are plain useQuery calls that throw into an ErrorBoundary on any server error. Never mount CollabDocEditor (DocumentDetailLayout's default edit mode), WatchButton, TaskDetailContent, PlanDetailPanel, ActivityFeed, or the tasks, docs and plans pages.
- Routing: next/navigation and next/link are shims over react-router (tsconfig.json:32-37, src/compat/*). The landing page already renders inside the router and the Convex/auth Providers (src/providers.tsx:143), so useRouter and Link work without extra providers. Clicks would navigate the visitor away, so pass onNavigate or no-op handlers.
- Layout gotcha: most TaskRow and DocRow columns carry `cq-hide-compact` / `cq-hide-minimal`. These are @container queries (globals.css:20,49: hidden under 600px and 350px of container width), and the nearest container is `.cq-container` (container-type: inline-size). Lay the surface out at real app width (for example 900px wide) inside a .cq-container and scale it with a CSS transform, which does not change layout width. Otherwise the chips vanish.
- Bundle gotcha: TaskRow and KanbanCard live in app/tasks/page.tsx and DocRow lives in app/docs/page.tsx. Importing them pulls whole page modules (TaskDetailContent, DashboardLayout, AuthGuard, GenericListView, feeders) into the lazy Landing chunk. Recommended refactor (a pure move with no behavior change): components/tasks/TaskRow.tsx (TaskRow, KanbanCard, PRIORITY_CONFIG, SubtaskRing), components/docs/DocRow.tsx, and export the GenericListView row shell as a ListRowShell. The product and the hero then share one copy, following the reuse rule. Also export DOC_MD_COMPONENTS (DocumentDetailLayout.tsx:31) and DaySection (ActivityFeed.tsx:407). Consider optional props to hide DocumentDetailLayout's ContextChatInput and to lift PlanTaskSection's and PlanBoardView's mutations into props.
- Existing hero: app/(marketing)/heroFly/surfaces.tsx and productMocks.tsx hand-build TaskRow, DocsMock and other mocks that "mirror" the real components (productMocks.tsx:341,374,414). These are the placeholders the user wants replaced.
- Unverified: the ThemeProvider-over-ForceLightMode effect-order issue is inferred from reading the code, not checked in a browser. Load / as a dark-theme signed-in user and check document.documentElement.className to confirm.

theme:
The whole SPA, marketing included, loads app/globals.css from src/main.tsx:2. The --sol-* tokens default to Solarized Light on :root (globals.css:326+, --sol-bg #FBF5E2, --sol-text #002b36). `.dark` (:387) and `.minimal-style` (:407, white #ffffff and #1f1f1f text) override them on <html>. Components get their colour from Tailwind sol-* classes that resolve to those variables. The exceptions noted in memory: text-sol-blue, bg-sol-cyan, violet and yellow accent classes are hardcoded Solarized hex, and GlobalSearch's result rows use raw amber, blue and emerald Tailwind classes.

The marketing route mounts MarketingLayout (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx). There, ForceLightMode (components/force-light-mode.tsx) removes `dark` and adds `light` to <html>, and the scroll container is `.light` with a hardcoded #fdf6e3 background, which differs slightly from --sol-bg #FBF5E2. So real components render correctly in light mode on the homepage.

Gap 1: ForceLightMode does not clear `minimal-style`. ThemeProvider (components/ThemeProvider.tsx:72-77) toggles it on <html> from localStorage or the server visual_style, so a signed-in user on the minimal style would see the hero's real components in the white/grey minimal palette. Either strip minimal-style in ForceLightMode, or wrap the hero in an element that re-declares the Solarized light --sol-* values so the hero is self-themed.

Gap 2: the build-time prerender (src/prerender-entry.tsx:70) renders marketing with only Convex auth providers and a MemoryRouter. There is no ThemeProvider, no ShortcutProvider and no TooltipProvider, so hero components must not require the shortcut or theme context during SSR. The leaves listed here do not; CommandPalette and GlobalSearch do.

The existing hero surfaces (app/(marketing)/heroFly/surfaces.tsx: PaletteSurface :438, BlameSurface :498, PageSurface :537) are hand-built mocks with hardcoded hex constants (INK, DIM, BODY). These are the placeholders to replace.
notes:
Isolation. inboxStore is a module singleton with no provider (the tests substitute the module; see components/__tests__/mockInboxStore.ts). A marketing-page component therefore cannot get a private fixture store, and any store write action (triggerAction, markNotificationRead, updateTask, and so on) lands in the signed-in user's real store, IDB and outbox, and dispatches to Convex. The safe rule is: compose the hero only from leaves whose inputs are props, give every click a local handler, and never mount the top-level containers (CommandPalette, GlobalSearch, NotificationBell, TriggersPage, BlobContent, PublishedPageEmbed), because each of them fires live queries and some write to the store (NotificationBell's useConvexSync syncTable).

Reuse refactors that make this clean, all small, each giving one shared implementation instead of a hero copy:
1. Move groupClass and itemClass out of CommandPalette.tsx:2317-2318 into a shared module.
2. Extract the palette's recent-session row (:2860-2918) and search-result row (:2940-3010) into exported components.
3. Extract GlobalSearch's result block (:395-455) into a SearchResultRow shared with app/search/page.tsx.
4. Lift the bell's dropdown frame into a presentational NotificationList.
5. Add an `actions` override (or a pure-render mode) to TriggerRowItem so verbs can drive local state.
6. Add a personifyAll override to SessionGlyph to match SessionIdentityLine.
7. Export PageCard from PublishedPageEmbed.tsx and HorizonRail from app/triggers/page.tsx.

Interactivity available with no server:
- cmdk filters and ranks fixture items as the visitor types (paletteItemScore is pure). Omit autoFocus so the page does not steal focus.
- highlightMatch re-highlights snippets live.
- SessionBlameStrip hover and pin lights lines in BlobView.
- ShortcutTooltip hovers on trigger rows work, since it carries its own provider.
- The published-page bar's comments panel works inside a sandboxed srcdoc iframe fed by a data: metaUrl, with fetch stubbed. The iframe also gives style isolation for free.

Other hazards:
- AvatarImg writes remote avatar bytes into the shared Cache Storage 'codecast:avatars:v1'. Prefer null avatars (initials fallback) or same-origin images.
- RoleHoverCard fires api.org.roleCard on hover for role rows.
- The timeAgo, useCoarseNow and relTimeShort clocks read Date.now, so fixture timestamps should be relative to the render time to keep 'now' and '3w ago' stable.
- Toasts go to the app Toaster mounted in src/providers.tsx.

No dedicated 'cast why' view exists in web. Blame lives only in components/repo (SessionBlame, BlobView) on /repo and /r.

The /a/<slug> viewer is not React. It is Convex-served HTML (artifactsHttp.ts serve, artifactPages.ts), so 'the real UI' there means calling brandArtifactHtml itself, ideally at build time into a static file under public/, to keep marked and highlight.js out of the web bundle.

Needs a ConvexProvider (present on the marketing page, which calls useConvexAuth). KeyCap from KeyboardShortcutsHelp; formatToolName from @codecast/shared/render (pure). The hero then renders PermissionStackView with fixture rows and local useState handlers (Approve moves to an 'approved' state and the row disappears, which is what the product does). components.name: iOS push banner content (Permission needed)
components.role: Defines what the real push says, for a faithful lock-screen/banner rendering. The daemon creates the notification with title 'codecast - Permission needed' and message = the command or reason truncated to 200 chars (daemon.ts:19665-19672; same title at :10995, :29028, :29965). Server delivery: convex/convex/notifications.ts:34-110 sends title, optional iOS subtitle, body, badge (the bell's unread count), sound 'default', interruptionLevel 'time-sensitive' for addressed types (pushRouter.ts:490 includes permission_request). There are NO Approve/Deny action buttons on the permission push: the only actionable category registered in the app is the huddle ring, Join/Decline (mobile/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:211-225). Tapping the banner opens the session, where the PermissionCard above is shown.
components.deps: None for rendering; this is the copy spec.
components.howToRender: Build a web iOS notification banner: app icon, 'CODECAST' app label, 'now', bold title 'codecast - Permission needed' (or 'Permission needed' if the app title is stripped by iOS grouping; the literal wire title includes the 'codecast - ' prefix), body = the command. Do not draw Approve/Deny buttons on the banner; the honest flow is banner -> tap -> session with the PermissionCard. Also available as real phone chrome: the Live Activity / Dynamic Island strip (mobile/targets/widget/CodecastLiveActivity.swift, StripViews.swift, Palette.swift) is always dark #002b36 with JetBrains Mono and status tints working=cyan, waiting=amber, done=green, failed=red. It is SwiftUI, so it would need a web recreation from those values.

theme: The web app's colours come from --sol-* CSS variables in packages/web/app/globals.css: light values on :root (globals.css:326+, e.g. --sol-bg #FBF5E2, --sol-text #002b36) and dark values on a .dark CLASS selector (globals.css:387+, --sol-bg #002b36, --sol-text #fdf6e3). Tailwind maps sol-bg/bg-alt/card/border/text* to those variables through color-mix so opacity modifiers work (tailwind.config.ts:18-26, 65-76). The accent colours (sol-yellow, green, red, blue, orange and so on) are hardcoded Solarized hex (tailwind.config.ts:47-64) and look the same in both themes. The marketing page loads the same globals.css, because src/main.tsx:2 imports it for the whole SPA. MarketingLayout (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx:21-22) mounts ForceLightMode, which puts 'light' on <html>, and wraps the page in a div with class 'light' and a #fdf6e3 background. So real components render in the correct light theme on the marketing page. Because .dark is a plain class selector and not html.dark, wrapping the phone subtree in <div className="dark"> redefines every --sol-* variable locally, and the real components will paint in true dark mode inside the phone while the page stays light. The mobile app defaults to Solarized, and its PermissionCard is hardcoded dark, so the phone should use that .dark wrapper. Caveat 1: ForceLightMode removes only dark/light. It does not remove 'minimal-style' (ThemeProvider.tsx:77), so a signed-in visitor using the minimal visual style gets the minimal token overrides on the marketing page too (.minimal-style at globals.css:406+, .dark.minimal-style at :469+). Scope the hero with its own class, or strip minimal-style in ForceLightMode. Caveat 2: the phone-layout CSS is written against the viewport, not the container: @media (max-width: 767px) at globals.css:1341-1398, and useIsPhone at 768px (hooks/useIsPhone.ts:6). Inside a 300px phone card on a desktop page, none of it fires, and md:/sm: Tailwind variants still resolve to desktop. A real web-phone layout would need an iframe with its own viewport.
notes:
Bottom line for the phone surface: no web component renders the iOS app, and the RN code cannot be dropped onto the page. packages/mobile does depend on react-native-web ~0.21 (package.json:69) and has an Expo web script (`expo start --web`, package.json:10), but the mobile components pull expo-haptics, expo-router, @expo/vector-icons, PanResponder gestures, Convex and the web inboxStore. packages/web has no react-native alias. Mounting them would mean either a second bundler config or an iframe to an Expo web export. That export is unverified: I did not run it, and native-only modules would likely break it. Not recommended for the hero.

Recommended approach:
1. For the permission beat, refactor web PermissionCard.tsx so the JSX becomes an exported presentational view. PermissionRow (:49) and ToolName (:16) are already pure; the single-permission body (:222-275) needs lifting out. PermissionStack keeps the useMutation (:121), the store write resolveSessionQuestion (:122, :133-138) and the global y/n keydown listener (:185-200). The hero renders the view with local state. That is real product UI with safe clicks. Mounting the current PermissionStack on the marketing page has three problems: it sends a real mutation with a fake id, it can write into a signed-in visitor's live store, and it approves or denies on any bare y/n keypress anywhere on the page.
2. The phone's in-app permission card should be a web twin of packages/mobile/components/PermissionCard.tsx, built from its StyleSheet (:113-190). Better still, hoist that style object into a shared module both platforms import. The web PermissionStack is the desktop card and looks different: slim, bordered, with KeyCaps. Use it on the desk surface, not the phone.
3. NotificationRow (components/notifications/NotificationRow.tsx:76) is props-only and safe today. It can be the phone's Notifications tab or the landing row after the push. It only reads the store (personify setting through SessionGlyph -> usePersonifyAll) and writes nothing.
4. Push banner copy must match the wire: title 'codecast - Permission needed', body = the command (daemon.ts:19665-19672), time-sensitive, with no action buttons. The only actionable push category is the huddle Join/Decline (usePushNotifications.ts:211-225). The current placeholder banner at heroFly/surfaces.tsx:280-291 is close, but its title and any implied banner buttons should follow this.
5. The existing placeholder to replace is PhoneSurface in app/(marketing)/heroFly/surfaces.tsx:223-293 plus PhoneFrame in productMocks.tsx:478-489. The fly() animation hooks there (phone/approve, phone/approved, phone/tapRing, phone/banner) need to survive, so wrap the real components in the fly() spans rather than handing fly props to them.
6. Precedent for rendering real components over fixtures already exists: preview/org-entry.tsx (it imports globals.css and toggles .dark), and vite.preview-migrate.config.ts:18-47 (it aliases inboxStore, convex/react and the generated api to preview/mocks/*). That alias trick is fine for a standalone preview bundle. It is not safe on the live marketing route, where signed-in visitors share one module graph with the real store, so the presentational-view split is the route that works there.

theme:
The app's colours are CSS custom properties defined in packages/web/app/globals.css: the `:root` block (line 326) is Solarized light (--sol-bg #FBF5E2, --sol-card #fff, --sol-text #002b36, accents), `.dark` (387) swaps to Solarized dark, and `.minimal-style` (407, plus `.dark.minimal-style` at 469-479) swaps to a white or neutral palette and changes --font-ui to SF Pro. Tailwind maps bg-sol-*/text-sol-* to those vars through themed() (tailwind.config.ts:65-75), with darkMode:["class"] (line 28). Per project memory, the accent utility classes (text-sol-blue, bg-sol-cyan, ...) are hardcoded hex rather than var().

globals.css IS loaded on the marketing page: src/main.tsx:2 imports it for every route. The marketing routes also sit inside the full app <Providers> (src/providers.tsx:146: ThemeProvider, ShortcutProvider, Convex auth root, Toaster), under MarketingLayout (src/App.tsx:168).

Light mode on marketing is not guaranteed for signed-in viewers:
(1) MarketingLayout mounts <ForceLightMode/> (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx:21), which sets html.light (components/force-light-mode.tsx:5-7). But ThemeProvider renders null until mounted (ThemeProvider.tsx:90), and in the commit where it flips to mounted, React runs the child effect (ForceLightMode) BEFORE the parent effect, so ThemeProvider's [theme, mounted] effect (line 54) then puts the viewer's stored theme back on <html>. A dark-mode user very likely ends up with html.dark on the landing page (this needs a browser check). It is invisible today because the marketing page uses hardcoded hex colours, but every real component (all --sol-* driven) would render dark on the cream page.
(2) ForceLightMode never removes `minimal-style` (ThemeProvider.tsx:77), so a user on the minimal visual style gets white surfaces and the SF Pro font in the film.
(3) ThemeProvider writes the viewer's bubble hue onto the root (line 45), which tints UserPrompt bubbles.
(4) The `className=\"light\"` on the marketing scroll div (MarketingLayout.tsx:22) does nothing: globals.css has no `.light` token block.
(5) Components that read useTheme() rather than CSS (WorkflowGraphView.tsx:130/331, ActivityHeatmap.tsx:45) take the viewer's context theme.

Fix for the film:
- Wrap the stage in a scope class that re-declares the :root light token block. Make it one shared selector (`:root, .sol-light-scope { ... }`) so there is no duplicated token list. Because custom properties inherit, this overrides html.dark and .minimal-style inside the stage, and it also resets --font-ui and the bubble hue var.
- Wrap the stage in a ThemeContext.Provider with value {theme:'light', visualStyle:'classic'}. ThemeContext is not exported today (ThemeProvider.tsx:17), so export it or add a tiny ForceThemeContext.
- Fonts: JetBrains Mono comes from --font-mono and the app's font loading, so it renders on marketing.
- Cast-canvas (HtmlSnippet) inherits var(--sol-*) from the host, so it follows the same scope.

ISOLATION FINDINGS (these decide the architecture)
1. There is no store seam. useInboxStore is a module singleton (store/inboxStore.ts:12843), useTrackedStore subscribes straight to it (12954), and importing the module starts IDB hydration and write-through (bootPersistence at 13459-13471; PERSISTENCE_AVAILABLE is simply `typeof window !== 'undefined'`, store/idbCache.ts:34). Fixture rows must therefore never be written into the store. Any component that reads it shows the real viewer's currentUser, teamMembers and clientState, and any action() or sync() it calls writes to the real store and IDB, and for action() to dispatch and the server.
   - A same-origin iframe does not isolate this: it shares the origin's IndexedDB.
   - A `sandbox=\"allow-scripts\"` iframe (opaque origin) would isolate it, but it would load the whole app bundle, and localStorage reads in ThemeProvider.tsx:21 would throw.
   - The cheap, honest route is to extract props-only View layers at the seams named above (SessionCardView, TaskRowView, and exporting PermissionRow) and let the existing components become store glue around them. That also satisfies the reuse rule: product and film render the same view.
2. Entity pills leak. Any id-shaped string (ct-123, pl-4, tr-9, jx7abcd, doc:...) in fixture markdown or props goes through useEntityResolution (lib/entityDisplay.ts:170-231) and fires real Convex queries. Anonymous visitors get null. A signed-in viewer sees their own real rows under those short ids. Two fixes: keep fixtures id-free, or add an override context in useEntityResolution that returns fixture rows (a small seam that makes TaskPill and SessionPill real).
3. Global keyboard handlers.
   - PermissionStack binds window y/n (PermissionCard.tsx:188-201) to a real mutation plus the store's resolveSessionQuestion. Never mount it on marketing.
   - ChatMessage binds document keydown and mousedown (271-272) for its menus. Harmless.
   - HtmlSnippet binds Escape only in fullscreen.
4. Error blast radius. Plain useQuery throws on server errors, and on marketing the only boundary is ErrorBoundary name=\"MarketingPage\" around the whole Outlet (MarketingLayout.tsx:23). Wrap the film in its own ErrorBoundary so a film failure cannot blank the landing page.
5. Router and next/* imports. next/link and next/navigation resolve to src/compat (vite.shared.ts:23-24) over react-router. Marketing is inside the Router, so Link and useRouter work, but clicks navigate for real. Film components should get no hrefs, or have clicks prevented at the stage root.
6. Safe as-is: the pure components tagged 'yes' above (chat, PR, blame, canvas, constellation, workflow graph, plan graph, diffs, presence, faces minus FaceRow, capability, vault, notification, integration).
7. Prior art for fixture rendering exists in gitignored harnesses: packages/web/_chatx.tsx (chat fixtures), __harness.faces.tsx (faces with the real tokens), plus _membercard, _peoplex, _diffx and _chatpage. These are the templates for film fixtures.

theme:
How colour reaches these components: they are styled with Tailwind classes such as bg-sol-card, text-sol-text and border-sol-border. tailwind.config.ts:65-75 maps those classes to var(--sol-*), and darkMode is set to ["class"] (:28). The variables are declared in packages/web/app/globals.css: light (Solarized Light) on :root at :326-386 (--sol-bg #FBF5E2, --sol-card #ffffff), dark on .dark at :387+, and a white/SF Pro palette on .minimal-style at :408+ (plus .dark.minimal-style at :474). Some accent classes are hardcoded Solarized hex rather than vars (per project memory: text-sol-blue, violet, yellow, cyan). Surface CSS comes from each component's own import: chat.css, decisions.css, faces.css, faceRow.css, people.css, presence.css, roomThread.css, walkie.css.

Does the marketing page get it? Yes. globals.css is imported once by src/main.tsx:2 for every route, and the landing page is a lazy route inside the same Providers tree (src/App.tsx:163-169), so ThemeProvider, ShortcutProvider, CodecastAuthRoot and the Convex client are all mounted there too. MarketingLayout (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx:19-21) mounts <ForceLightMode/>, which swaps html's dark class for light (components/force-light-mode.tsx:5-6). It also wraps the page in a div with class "light" and an inline #fdf6e3 background.

Three ways the light theme can fail for a signed-in visitor:
1. The ".light" class defines no variables. There is no .light { } block, so the wrapper div resets nothing, and any .dark on html cascades straight through.
2. ThemeProvider re-applies the stored theme. Its effect (components/ThemeProvider.tsx:50-56, a plain useEffect via hooks/useWatchEffect.ts) runs after its children's effects in the same commit, and again whenever clientState.ui.theme syncs in. So a dark-theme user can end up with html.dark on the landing page after ForceLightMode has run. I traced this from the code but have not reproduced it in a browser.
3. ForceLightMode never removes minimal-style. A user on the minimal visual style gets the white/SF Pro palette on real components. This one is certain from the code.

Fix: give the hero world root its own class that re-declares the :root light --sol-* block and sets color-scheme: light. The components would then paint Solarized Light no matter what html carries. Tailwind dark: variants key off any .dark ancestor, so html.dark would still flip those; audit or avoid dark: utilities inside the hero. CallStage shows the scoping works: it pins its own palette by putting .dark on its portal root (CallStage.tsx:301-305).
notes:
Short version: the chat timeline, the decision option and answer rows, the staffing pane, transcript turns, face circles and the identity faces render correctly from fixtures today. The permission card, face row, calls, composer and every queue/page container need small extractions or must be avoided, because their clicks and hovers act on the signed-in user's real data.

Read-only survey; I edited no files.

**What is already in the tree**
- The current hero (app/(marketing)/HeroFlythrough.tsx, heroFly/surfaces.tsx) is 100% hand-built mocks. It imports only react plus its own timeline and world modules (surfaces.tsx:11-43).
- Fixture paths already exist:
  - packages/web/_chatx.tsx mounts ChatMessageList, ChatMessage, ChatChannelRail and ChatToast from fixtures with only globals.css (gitignored scratch file).
  - __harness.faces.tsx renders FaceCircle and FacesChrome to static markup with the real tokens.
  - components/org/orgFixture.ts and orgStaffingFixture.ts are typed, deterministic org trees and proposals, already used by OrgPage's ?preview=1 mode and by the StaffingPane mount/fit tests.
  - chat/chatTypes.ts says outright that its view models are "Deliberately independent of the store row shapes" so they render from fixtures.

**Leak and side-effect hazards (the ones that matter)**
1. **Approve on the permission card.** PermissionStack (components/PermissionCard.tsx:121) sends `useMutation(api.permissions.updatePermissionStatus)` to Convex with the fixture id (errors swallowed). It also calls the store's resolveSessionQuestion and adds a window keydown listener (:185). The fix is to export the pure PermissionRow (:49) and use that.
2. **Answering a decision.** `answerDecision` (store/inboxStore.ts:8405-8443) is an action() that edits sessionDecisions and then runs addOptimisticMessage + sendMessage into the real outbox. It is a no-op for ids not in the store, so a fixture card cannot leak, but it also shows nothing. Drive fixture cards through DecisionAnswerControls' `onAnswer` callback, which only builds the answer input and calls back (DecisionAnswerControls.tsx:17-20).
3. **Typing into any real composer.** ChatComposer and RoomThread both embed MessageInput. It writes drafts through `setDraft`, a sync() that writes both drafts[id] and clientState.drafts[id] (inboxStore.ts:10899-10903), so fixture text lands in the signed-in user's IDB and clientState. The chat typing hooks do skip non-Convex ids (hooks/useChatTyping.ts:55,:92). Fake the palette/composer typing beat, or add a store-isolation seam first.
4. **Hovering a face.** useFaceKey (presence/useFaceKey.ts:167-181) calls `prewarmRoom(dmRoomKey)` after a dwell, which opens a real LiveKit connection as the viewer. Holding a face calls openDmChannel. Pass callsEnabled={false}, which blocks both, and/or set pointer-events:none on the seats.
5. **window.__faceRow.fake.** It is a module-global override shared by every face-row reader in the window (lib/faces/faceRow.ts:790-797, :853), and it only fakes the walkie, the announcement and input patches: the roster still comes from the real inboxStore. Use `deriveFaceRow(fixtureInput, null)` (faceRow.ts:473, a pure function of FaceRowInput at :183) and pass the result as FaceRow's `row` prop.
6. **Queries on fixture ids.** These all use useQueryNoThrow, so they tolerate fixture ids but still send a request:
   - OptionPages → artifacts.getShared
   - RoleHoverCard on hover → org.roleCard
   - CallTranscriptDisclosure → transcripts
   - useStorageImageSrc for chat attachments (batch storage-URL queries)
   - EntityAware markdown pills for ct-/jx7 ids in fixture text

   Keep fixtures free of attachments, report slugs, workflow_run_id, task_id and stack_id, and short ids in prose.
7. **Portals escape the 3D world.** Radix Tooltip and Popover portal to document.body (components/ui/tooltip.tsx:16, popover.tsx:16), and so does CallStage (a fixed inset-0 portal). Anything opened on hover renders flat and screen-positioned instead of inside the transformed world.
8. **Navigation.** next/link and next/navigation resolve to the react-router shims (vite.shared.ts:23-24, src/compat). They work on the marketing route, but a click leaves the page. useJumpToDecisionAsk falls back to window.location.assign.
9. **Avatar cache.** AvatarImg caches avatar bytes in the Cache Storage bucket 'codecast:avatars:v1' (lib/avatarCache.tsx:34), which the signed-in app shares. It is harmless, but use same-origin /public images for fixture avatars.

**Recommended extractions (small, reuse-first)**
- Export PermissionRow.
- Split DecisionCompactCard into a props-only DecisionCompactCardView fed by the current wrapper.
- Export RoomThread's RecapCard, PassageBlock and ChatLine.
- Export CallStage's AudioOnlyStage, VoiceRows and CaptionsLane with roster props.
- Pull FaceSeat's circle into a props-only view.

Each keeps one rendering path for the app and the hero.

**Org chart caveat**
OrgGraph is React Flow. It measures nodes and fits its own viewport, so give it an untransformed fixed-size inner box and scale the parent, not the canvas.

theme:
The CSS loads on the marketing page. The theme is only reliably light for anonymous visitors.

- **Stylesheet.** app/globals.css is imported by the SPA entry (src/main.tsx:2), so every route, the marketing page included, gets the --sol-* variables. :root is Solarized Light (globals.css:326-385) and .dark overrides it (:387+). Tailwind maps sol-bg, sol-text, sol-card, sol-border and the muted/dim text colours to var(--sol-*) via color-mix (tailwind.config.ts:65-75), and darkMode is 'class' (:28). The accent classes (text-sol-violet, bg-sol-cyan and so on) are hardcoded Solarized hex (tailwind.config.ts:61), so accents never follow a theme.
- **How the marketing page forces light.** MarketingLayout (src/layouts/MarketingLayout.tsx:21-22) mounts ForceLightMode (components/force-light-mode.tsx), which strips `dark` from <html> on mount and adds `light`. The wrapper div's `light` class does nothing, because globals.css has no .light variable block.
- **Risk 1, dark users (plausible, needs checking in a browser).** ThemeProvider (components/ThemeProvider.tsx:50-56) re-adds the user's stored theme class to <html> whenever `theme` or `mounted` changes. React runs child passive effects before parent ones, so in the commit where ThemeProvider first renders its children, its effect can run after ForceLightMode's and put `dark` back. It will also re-apply dark whenever clientState.ui.theme syncs in and differs from the initial value. Product components then render dark on the cream marketing page.
- **Risk 2, minimal style (certain from the code).** ForceLightMode never removes `minimal-style`. For a user on the minimal visual style, .minimal-style (globals.css:407+) swaps --sol-bg to #ffffff and --font-ui to SF Pro, so product components render white and sans-serif inside the hero.
- **Components that ignore CSS variables.** WorkflowGraphView picks a hardcoded palette from useTheme().theme (:331), the viewer's stored theme, so it goes dark for dark users whatever the html class says. With no provider it defaults to light.
- **Page-scoped CSS.** pr.css and repo.css are imported only by their route modules and must be imported explicitly by the hero.
- **Fix.** Scope the hero in its own root that re-declares the light :root values and removes the minimal-style overrides, e.g. a `.hero-light` class that copies the :root --sol-* block and --font-ui. Also give WorkflowGraphView a way to be told the theme.
notes:
I edited no files.

**1. The store can't be sandboxed.** useInboxStore is a module singleton (store/inboxStore.ts:12843) with no React context seam. Any component that calls useInboxStore, useTrackedStore or useCollectionRows reads the signed-in viewer's live store, and every store action writes to it and dispatches to Convex. There are two options:
- Only mount leaves that take props, and block pointer events.
- Add a store-provider seam: a context-selected fixture store that useTrackedStore and useInboxStore consult first. That is a large change.

**2. EntityIdPill leaks real data and is the single biggest blocker.** Trigger blocks, worker reports, cast rows, PR linked sessions and commit links all go through it. useEntityResolution (lib/entityDisplay.ts:170-231) always runs live Convex queries and seeds from the real store. Fixture ids like tr-12, ct-4102 or a 7-character jx prefix will resolve to a signed-in viewer's REAL trigger, task or session and show its real title in the hero. For an anonymous visitor they fall back to the raw id or plain text.
- Fix: one seam in EntityIdPill/useEntityResolution, e.g. an EntityFixtureContext that returns a fixture entity and passes 'skip' to every query. It covers every surface on this list at once.
- Without it, avoid entity ids in fixtures, or use shapes that can't match.

**3. Clicks and keys escape the hero.** Every Link in these components really navigates, because src/compat/next-link.tsx uses react-router's navigate. Handlers call real store actions: triggerAction, requestNavigate, navigateToSession, updateClientUI, patchConversation, answerDecision. ForkTreeContent and BrowserPane add window keydown listeners in the capture phase.
- Any interactive fixture needs a capture-phase click interceptor on the hero root, or pointer-events:none except on elements the hero wires itself.
- Safe interactions: local useState toggles (ScheduledTaskBlock folds, WorkflowContextPanel expand, ThreadStatePanel 'Show all') and hover rails.

**4. Prerender gap (inferred, not checked).** src/prerender-entry.tsx wraps pages in Convex providers and a MemoryRouter only. There is no ThemeProvider, ShortcutProvider or TipProvider. useTheme and useTipActions have safe defaults. Whether the inboxStore module (IDB and dispatch set up at import) loads safely under renderToString for the marketing route has not been tested.

**5. Time-relative rendering.** useCoarseNow reads Date.now(). Relative ages, countdowns and ThreadStatePanel's cutoff (it renders null once the pin is stale) mean fixture timestamps must be offsets from now. That will make prerendered text differ from what hydration produces unless the timeline freezes the time.

**6. Where it stands today.** The current hero (app/(marketing)/heroFly/surfaces.tsx) is built from productMocks.tsx, hand-built look-alikes. notes:
Bottom line: nothing today lets a store-bound component render fixtures safely on the homepage. There is one store, `useInboxStore` (store/inboxStore.ts:12843), and nothing provides a second one through context. On the marketing route that store is fully live, because src/boot.tsx:11 imports it and bootPersistence (L13471) binds IDB write-through and the durable outbox for every page.

**How fixture data would leak if it went into the real store:**
1. **action() calls.** Clicking Approve on a real permission card calls something like `useInboxStore.getState().<action>()`. That writes the real draft, persists it to IDB, and enqueues it in the durable outbox even though nothing is dispatching on this route (platform/packages/engine/src/middleware.ts:1119-1150). useEnsureDispatch drains the outbox the next time the user opens /inbox, so the write reaches the server late.
2. **syncTable/setState seeding.** Seeded fixtures reach IDB through write-through. Other tabs then see them when they hydrate.
3. **Pending messages.** persistPendingMessageChanges runs in the middleware wrapper on every set, for any store instance (store/mutativeMiddleware.ts:373 -> store/idbCache.ts:178). It writes to localStorage and to IDB under the current user.
4. **Gestures.** broadcastGesture in hide, forget and follow actions can hide rows in the user's other open app tabs.
5. **Convex queries.** The marketing route sits inside the real authenticated Convex client (src/providers.tsx:127, lib/authRoot.tsx:22). A fixture id passed to useQuery either throws in render (v.id validation, then the ErrorBoundary) or opens a real prod subscription. useQueryNoThrow turns the error into a value but still subscribes.
6. **Analytics.** track() calls inside real components fire real analytics events once analytics has initialized.

Sync-host replication and dispatch binding are NOT mounted on marketing: they live only in DashboardLayout (components/DashboardLayout.tsx:315-326), and the palette, people and call pages also bind dispatch.

**Why a second instance in the same page is only half-isolated.** A fresh createInboxStore() gets its own middleware closures, so no IDB writer, outbox or dispatch unless bound (all bindings happen in hydrateInboxCacheFromIDB, L13181). But:
- 229 files under components/, hooks/ and lib/ reach the store imperatively with useInboxStore.getState/setState/subscribe, and those always hit the singleton;
- about 14 action bodies inside the store config also read the singleton or the `store` proxy;
- module-level side effects (pending journal, localStorage prefs, gesture channel) are shared.

So "add a StoreContext and point useTrackedStore at it" (about 3 hook sites) would make reads consistent but leave clicks writing to the real store. Threading context through 229 imperative call sites is a large, risky refactor. I would reject it.

**Recommendation, in order of preference:**

**A. Default: render the presentational layer with fixture props, in the page's own realm.**
- Where a component mixes data and view, split it into a container (store/Convex reads plus actions) and a props-only view. The product renders the container and the hero renders the view.
- Interactions such as Approve, hover or palette typing become local useState in the hero, driven by the timeline.
- This is the preview/org-entry.tsx pattern (real RoleCard over fixture props) and needs zero store contact.
- It also prerenders correctly, which the spec's POSTER_T frame requires. Store-seeded data does not prerender, because zustand serves getInitialState under renderToString.
- Wrap the hero in a nested `<ConvexProvider client={stub}>` whose watchQuery returns fixtures or undefined and whose mutation and action are no-ops. That neutralises any stray useQuery/useMutation inside the tree; the stub needs no socket.
- Wrap it in a ShortcutProvider scope, or pass disabled flags, so palette shortcuts do not register on the page.
- Cost: roughly 0.5 to 2 hours per component split, plus about 1 hour for the stub Convex client and wrapper. This is also a good refactor for the product.

**B. Only for trees too large to split (the full ConversationView or the inbox list): a sandbox realm.**
- Load the hero in an iframe from a dedicated entry, modelled on packages/web/preview/*.html but built for production as a second Vite input.
- Inside the iframe, the real inboxStore module is a separate singleton, so all 229 imperative sites automatically hit the sandbox store. The fixtures seed through the real syncTable and actions, so the result looks exactly like the product.
- The iframe is same-origin by default, so it still shares IDB, localStorage and BroadcastChannel. Two ways to close that:
  - **Preferred:** serve the entry from a separate origin (for example a hero subdomain). Storage isolation is then structural.
  - **Otherwise:** add one sandbox flag, set before the store module is imported, that:
    - skips bootPersistence (L13471) and the window.__inboxStore handle (L12927);
    - skips persistPendingMessageChanges (mutativeMiddleware.ts:373) and the persistWorkspace/critical-prefs localStorage writes (L310, L332);
    - calls setGestureChannelFactory(() => null) (an existing seam, gestureBridge.ts:128);
    - calls `_setDispatch(async () => null)` (precedent: components/integrations/fixtures/issueSyncNavigation.tsx:35).
  - Also: mount the stub ConvexProvider, never mount Providers, ThemeProvider, GestureBridge or DashboardLayout, and never init analytics.
- An opaque-origin sandboxed iframe (no allow-same-origin) is stronger, but localStorage access throws there and many modules read it at import.
- Costs:
  - no prerender (show a poster image until the iframe paints);
  - the app bundle downloads for anonymous visitors;
  - the whole 3D world should live inside ONE iframe, with fixtures seeded through syncTable (the store must hold a currentUser and active_team_id, and rows need matching `workspace` stamps, or useWorkspaceCollection filters them out).
- Estimate: 1 to 2 days for the entry, the flag gates, a guard test that the sandbox realm never opens Dexie or posts to BroadcastChannel, and deploy wiring for the separate origin.

**Not recommended:**
- Branching per component on a preview flag, as OrgPage ?preview=1 does (DEV-only, OrgPage.tsx:74, 171-280). It needs one branch per action and per query.
- The faceRow fake (lib/faces/faceRow.ts:777-853). It fakes the store half by writing into the real __inboxStore.
- The preview/mocks hand-written stub store. Its useTrackedStore returns null, so real store-bound components break.

**Context:** the current HeroFlythrough (app/(marketing)/HeroFlythrough.tsx, heroFly/surfaces.tsx, spec heroFlythrough.spec.md, ct-55800) is uncommitted work from another session. It is built entirely on hand-made productMocks.tsx pieces, so it has no store or Convex contact today. Swapping those mocks for the real views from option A keeps that property.
